subject: Urgent: Production 503s + latency spike — Phoenix Specialty (us-west-2)
messages:
From: Aaron Cho <aaron.cho@phoenix-specialty.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@phoenix-specialty.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors: 503s and major latency spike in us-west-2

Neha —

Starting ~14:45 PST we began seeing a surge of 503s from Redwood on our production traffic (homepage and checkout routing) and p95 latency spiked from ~120ms to >900ms. Throughput to your endpoint dropped ~40% even though our request rate is steady. We've attached a short log snippet and a couple of example request IDs.

This is impacting a live campaign. Can you confirm whether this is an AZ-level problem or something on our side? We need an ETA for mitigation — if we can't get stable responses in the next 30–60m we may need to roll to our fallback text-model which has worse quality.

Attached: error_snippet.log (top 50 lines), sample_request_ids.txt

— Aaron
Head of Platform, Phoenix Specialty
aaron.cho@phoenix-specialty.com

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors: 503s and major latency spike in us-west-2

Aaron — thanks for flagging and apologies for the disruption. We’re on it. I’ve looped in Marissa (CSM), Alex (SE) and Rishi (on-call infra) and copied Lauren to keep leadership apprised.

Immediate asks for your team: can you share one failing request-id from the log and the approximate % of affected traffic (if you can see that)? That will help us target routing rules.

Our immediate mitigations we can activate while we triage:
- Shift Phoenix traffic away from us-west-2 (targeting us-west-1) for a temporary geo-handshake (expected < 20m to propagate)
- Enable a temporary model variant (redwood-base-8q) to reduce inference load if the route swap doesn’t fully mitigate
- Kick autoscaling on the DW pool serving your tenancy (we can force scale now)

I’ll send an internal escalation next with metrics and an exec-ready note — will follow up within 10m with an ETA.

— Neha
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: URGENT: Phoenix Specialty — us-west-2 503/latency spike (exec brief)

Team — escalating on behalf of Phoenix Specialty (PLAT-3489). They report widespread 503s and p95 latency ~900ms starting 14:45 PST. This is hitting prod Homepage/Checkout routes; initial impact estimate: ~35–45% of their requests. Aaron attached a small log excerpt (see attachment).

Observed in the dashboard (link below): increased 5xx rate from 0.1% -> 5.8%; throughput dip; queue depth for gw-proxy increased. Potential impact: renewal conversation on the table due to campaign downtime. Lauren is copied for executive visibility.

Please triage and propose immediate mitigations. Recommended immediate actions (prioritized):
1) Verify whether problem is localized to us-west-2b (AZ) or broader us-west-2. Check host-level network metrics and recent host maintenance windows.
2) If AZ-level and hosts degraded, initiate geo-reroute for Phoenix tenant to us-west-1 (route-by-tenant policy). Use warmup routing to avoid cold-KV issues.
3) Force an increase to request autoscaling for their Dedicated pool; if quota prevents, propose a temporary override for this account.
4) If routing change not effective within 20m, enable model fallback to redwood-base-8q and enable prefix caching.

Attachments: perf_snapshot.png, phoenix_action_plan.md
Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/phoenix-specialty/overview
HS ticket: HS-52347

I need a short, clear status update I can send to Aaron and a 1–2 line exec summary for Lauren within 10m.

— Neha

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:28:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Phoenix Specialty — us-west-2 503/latency spike (exec brief)

Neha/Team — quick triage update (15:28 PDT). Observations:
- Fault appears isolated to us-west-2b hosts in the serving pool for Phoenix; we’re seeing transient network congestion on 3 hosts that caused heavy KV-cache evictions and request queueing. No widespread control-plane faults.
- Metrics: host network retransmits up 12x, per-host load average spiking concurrent with GC/eviction events; 5xxs concentrated at the gateway layer before model runtime.

Immediate actions I’ve executed:
- Initiated tenant-level route override to steer Phoenix traffic to us-west-1 (warm-up routing enabled) — propagation underway (expected 8–18 minutes for edge to converge).
- Forced scale on the DW pool for Phoenix (+30% capacity) and temporarily raised burst limits for their dedicated pool.
- Instituted a protective rate-limit on non-critical background routes to free headroom for prod routes.

If we still see >1% 5xx after 20m, plan B is to flip Phoenix to the base-8q variant and enable persistent prefix caching for their tenant (will be a ~5–10m change with quality regression).

I’ll monitor and post another update in 10m. If any exec note is needed: "Root cause appears to be network saturation on a subset of us-west-2 hosts; traffic is being rerouted to us-west-1 while we remediate."

— Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production errors: 503s and major latency spike in us-west-2

Aaron — quick update and apology for the disruption.

What we did:
- We detected network saturation on a subset of us-west-2 hosts and routed Phoenix traffic to us-west-1; edge propagation completed ~15:40 PDT on 5/20.
- Forced extra capacity for your dedicated pool and applied a temporary protective rate limit to background routes.
- No code changes required; the immediate root cause appears infrastructure-level (host network saturation) and our on-call corrected the routing and scaled pools.

Current status (09:30 PDT 5/21):
- 5xx rates returned to baseline (~0.12%), p95 latency back to normal (~130ms).
- We are continuing to monitor your traffic for 24h and will publish a postmortem draft by EOD tomorrow. I’ve attached a working postmortem link.

Next steps for Phoenix team:
1) Confirm on your side that the errors have stopped and the user flows you were monitoring are healthy.
2) If you prefer, we can schedule a 30m sync to review the timeline and the longer-term hardening plan (cross-region warm caches, increased host redundancy).

Lauren (copied) has been briefed and is available if you want an executive call — we understand the impact to your campaign and apologize.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-link.txt

— Neha
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
